title: Anatomical Heart Emoji 🫀 Meaning: Love, Literally
description: The anatomical heart emoji 🫀 shows the real organ. It means cardiology and health, or love so intense it gets visceral. When 🫀 beats ❤️ and when it is too graphic.
summary: 🫀 depicts a real human heart, with chambers and blood vessels instead of the classic symbol. It is used for medicine, cardiology, CPR and heart health, and figuratively for raw emotion: love, heartbreak or pounding nerves expressed in a more intense, slightly unsettling way than ❤️.
meaning: Most heart emojis are symbols. 🫀 is an organ, and that difference shapes every use. In medical settings it is simply accurate: cardiologists, nursing students, CPR instructors and heart-health campaigns use it the way a textbook uses a diagram. It also suits personal news about heart conditions, surgeries or checkups, where a cartoon ❤️ would feel oddly cheerful.

Figuratively, 🫀 turns emotion into something visceral. “You have my whole 🫀” suggests love felt in the body rather than printed on a card. People use it for poems, tattoo ideas and captions that aim for raw sincerity. It also suits an aesthetic that blends romance with a little darkness, the kind associated with gothic and alternative style.

Humor is common as well. Fans post “my heart literally stopped” with 🫀 after a shocking plot twist, or send it when something makes their pulse race, such as a crush walking into the room. The anatomical detail makes the exaggeration funnier, because it pictures the actual organ struggling rather than a tidy valentine.

It was approved in 2020 and filled a gap for health conversations, which until then had to borrow symbolic hearts. Because it shows vessels and chambers, some people find it a bit graphic. Others like it for exactly that reason: it feels more honest and less sugary than the long row of colored hearts on the keyboard.

contexts.label: In health and medicine
contexts.body: Hospitals, clinics, nursing students and fitness accounts use 🫀 for cardiology, blood pressure, CPR training and heart-healthy habits. Patients share recovery updates after procedures with it. In these settings it reads as informative and serious, and it avoids the romantic associations a red heart would bring to a medical post.

contexts.label: In romance
contexts.body: Using 🫀 instead of ❤️ suggests love felt deeply and physically, as in “you make my 🫀 race.” Some find this intense and charming, while others think it is a little strange. It fits partners who share a dark sense of humor or an interest in anatomy, horror or gothic style.

contexts.label: In fandoms and reactions
contexts.body: Shocking episodes, emotional finales and swoon-worthy photos earn replies like “my 🫀 can’t take this.” The organ makes the reaction feel physical and dramatic. It often appears with 😭 or 💀, where the joke is that the viewer’s actual heart is struggling to keep up with what they just saw.

Expressing love that feels deep and physical.

combos.meaning: Doctors, checkups and cardiology; clearly medical.
Emotionally wrecked by something moving or shocking.
Intense, burning passion or a pounding heartbeat.
Dark romance aesthetic: love with an edge.

confusedWith.difference: ❤️ is the classic symbol of love, friendly enough for anyone. 🫀 is the organ itself and carries medical or intensely emotional meaning. Sending 🫀 where ❤️ is expected can come across as dramatic, funny or a little macabre.
💓 shows a symbolic pink heart with lines suggesting a heartbeat and excitement. 🫀 shows the anatomical organ. Both can mean a racing pulse, but 💓 stays cute while 🫀 feels raw.
🩸 is a single drop of blood, used for donation, menstruation and injury. It sometimes appears beside 🫀 in medical contexts, but it refers to blood itself rather than to the heart.

avoid: Avoid it in a sweet message to someone squeamish, who may find the realistic organ unpleasant.
Do not use it jokingly in conversations about someone’s real heart attack or illness.
design: A realistic human heart in reddish pink, showing its rounded chambers and the large blood vessels that branch from the top. Some designs color certain vessels blue to separate veins from arteries, echoing textbook diagrams. Styles range from soft and simplified to fairly detailed, but all clearly show the organ rather than the symbolic shape.

faqs.a: Either something about the actual heart, such as health news or a cardiology class, or a deeper, more dramatic version of love and emotion. “My 🫀” after a shocking moment means the sender’s heart is racing or breaking.

It can be, for people who like intensity. It suggests love felt in the body rather than a cute gesture. Some partners love it; others find it odd. If you are unsure how someone will react, a red heart is the safer choice.

❤️ is a symbol of affection that anyone can use casually. 🫀 is the real organ, so it suits medical topics or emotion pushed to an extreme. One is a valentine; the other is closer to an anatomy diagram.

faqs.q: When was the anatomical heart emoji released?
faqs.a: It was approved in 2020 as part of Emoji 13.0. Phones gained support through system updates after that, so a device that has not been updated in a long time may still show an empty box instead.
